name: Ferrogate Metro Bus
description: Forty-year-old electric buses running surface routes through Tier 1-3 districts. Overcrowded doesn't begin to describe it — during rush hour, riders hang from external grab rails and stand on bumper platforms that were never designed for passengers. The suspension is shot on most units. Air conditioning is a memory. But a bus pass is cheaper than the L-train, and the routes go where the rails don't.
propulsion: Electric motor, overhead catenary wire + battery backup
speed: Average 15 km/h in traffic, 30 km/h on dedicated lanes
range: 180 km on full charge, effectively unlimited on catenary routes
cost: Φ1 per ride, Φ30 monthly pass
autonomy: Human driver required. Autodrive disabled after the '91 routing hack.
common_usage: The absolute bottom tier of public transit. Used by those who can't afford the L or live in districts the rail doesn't serve.
story_hooks: A bus driver has been running an unofficial route through a dead zone for six years — the only transit link for an unregistered community
Someone is tagging buses with symbols that form a message only readable from the L-train platforms above
physical_description: A battered electric transit bus, its once-blue polymer hull now faded to slate gray under decades of acid rain and industrial grime. Rust blooms around the wheel wells and door frames; the windows are scratched milky from years of abrasion. Dents and impact scars map its flanks, and the grab rails—welded steel tubes—are worn smooth by ten thousand desperate hands. Flickering LED route displays barely function; the interior lighting flickers in rhythm with the dying battery pack.
